record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Generalize equivariant map superalgebras by allowing the target to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, replacing the commutative coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Γ by a Z2-graded group; then determine the resulting representation theory in this broader super setting.

evidence.quote: (c) Superschemes and superalgebras. The equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] can be naturally generalized. First, one can consider more general Lie superalgebras for the target g. For example, one could take any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra (not just basic classical ones). Furthermore, one can replace A by a supercommutative algebra (in other words, let X be a superscheme) and Γ by a Z2 -graded group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra over $\mathbb{C}$ (not necessarily basic classical). Let $A$ be a finitely generated supercommutative associative $\mathbb{C}$-superalgebra, and let $X = \operatorname{Spec} A$ be the corresponding (affine) superscheme. Let $\Gamma$ be a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded group acting by $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded automorphisms on both $A$ (equivalently $X$) and $\mathfrak{g}$. Define the equivariant map superalgebra
$$ (\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^\Gamma = \{ x \in \mathfrak{g} \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} A : \gamma \cdot x = x \text{ for all } \gamma \in \Gamma\}, $$
endowed with its natural Lie superalgebra structure inherited from the bracket $[u\otimes a, v\otimes b] = [u,v]\otimes ab$ (with appropriate signs).

Develop the representation theory of $(\mathfrak{g}\otimes A)^\Gamma$ in this generality. In particular:
(i) Classify the irreducible finite-dimensional (or, where appropriate, the irreducible integrable) modules of $(\mathfrak{g}\otimes A)^\Gamma$.
(ii) Describe such modules in terms of (twisted) evaluation modules associated to $\Gamma$-orbits of (rational) points of the superscheme $X$.
(iii) Determine the extensions between irreducible modules and the block decomposition of suitable categories of modules.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed special cases of this generalization. Equivariant map queer Lie superalgebras (a non-basic-classical simple Lie superalgebra target) were treated by Calixto–Savage (arXiv:1412.5098), classifying irreducible finite-dimensional modules under the assumption that $\Gamma$ is a finite abelian group acting freely on $X$. Further work (e.g., on irreducible modules and their extensions for equivariant map superalgebras) has appeared. However, the full program in the broadest setting—arbitrary finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra target, supercommutative $A$ (genuine superscheme $X$), and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded group $\Gamma$—does not appear to have been fully carried out, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant map queer Lie superalgebras
status_evidence.snippet: An equivariant map queer Lie superalgebra is the Lie superalgebra of regular maps from an algebraic variety (or scheme) X to a queer Lie superalgebra q that are equivariant with respect to the action of a finite group Γ. We classify irreducible finite-dimensional representations under the assumption that Γ is abelian and acts freely on X.
status_evidence.claim: The queer (non-basic-classical) target case is treated, but only with ordinary (not Z2-graded) Γ and with A commutative.

status_evidence.title: Irreducible modules for equivariant map superalgebras and their extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Classification and extensions for irreducible modules of equivariant map superalgebras in the basic classical setting.
status_evidence.claim: Further development of representation theory in the basic classical setting; full superscheme / Z2-graded group setting not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant map superalgebras
status_evidence.snippet: Original equivariant map superalgebra setting with basic classical g, commutative A, ordinary group Γ.
status_evidence.claim: Baseline setting that the proposed generalization extends.
